content.text: Unconstrained trees overfit. Use max_depth, min_samples_leaf, or pruning to regularise.

questions.question: What is overfitting in a decision tree?
options: The tree memorises training data and fails on new data
The tree takes too long to train
The tree has too few nodes
questions.explanation: Overfitting means the model fits the training data too closely and does not generalise.

faq.q: What is the difference between a decision tree and a random forest?
faq.a: A random forest is an ensemble of many decision trees, each trained on a random subset of data and features. It is much more accurate and less prone to overfitting.
